I have an interesting story about the placebo effect, actually.

In 2011 I got pregnant, and the antidepressant I was on was a class D, which means there is evidence it can harm a fetus. So I was put on Buspar, which has no known risk to a fetus. I thought, "Okay, so I'm set. I'm off the Paxil and on the Buspar." Well, within just a few weeks of making the switch the old symptoms were back. I was thinking of suicide more and more. I was exactly where I had been years before when I hadn't started taking anything yet. Finally I had enough and went back to the doctor.

Turns out Buspar is really good for anxiety only. It doesn't do much for depression. That's why I had backslid so much in such a short period of time. My depression was basically untreated again.

So in my case, I don't think it's placebo. If it were, then the Buspar would have done the trick as well as the Paxil because I was fully expecting it to.

I do think however they are too quick to prescribe antidepressants to people. As I said, the side effects are terrible and I wouldn't want to deal with them unless I had real need for the medication. If exercise and the like could treat my depression (believe me, I've tried) I'd happily do that because it would be less awful than the medication.
